leaderboards.title: Best AI coding agents
leaderboards.note: Scored tools ran our standard task between 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-06 (see the test write-up). The AI model differs between tools (Copilot: gpt-6-luna, Cursor CLI: Composer 2.5, Aider, Cline, Crush, Goose, Pi and Qwen Code: gemini-3.8-flash, Bolt.new: its Free-plan default, OpenCode: deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, Kilo Code: Auto Free). Pricing for Copilot was rechecked 2026-11-06.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.description: GitHub's AI coding assistant and agent for editors, the CLI and pull requests.

test.model: gpt-6-luna (Copilot Free default; Fusion auto-routed, only Free candidate for this task)
test.evidence: Retest on the latest CLI (1.0.105 on Oct 30 and 1.0.98 on Oct 15 both scored 99). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 48 s with no interventions on Copilot Free (0.46 AI credits). Single-file app validates saved data (Array + field checks, try/catch), uses textContent, labels the input, names the task on the delete button, and flips the checkbox aria-label between complete and incomplete. The Oct 15/30 −1 quality for a static "as complete" label is gone. Self-check: recovered from a missing `python` binary by retrying with `python3` and `node --check`.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.pricing: Free, open source; free models included, or bring your own model provider
tools.description: Open-source AI coding agent for the terminal, IDE and desktop, with built-in free models.

test.model: deepseek-v4.1-flash-free (OpenCode built-in free model, no account)
test.evidence: Retest (first test Oct 19 on 1.19.3 scored 93). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 96 s on the first try, with no interventions, no sign-in and no card. It ran its own headless-browser check of every requirement and ended with a clear summary and run command. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label doesn't name the task. -1 DX: the Oct 19 setup issues are still there in 1.19.5 (re-checked 2026-10-29): with no model set it auto-picks a provider from unrelated tokens in the environment, and 'opencode run' waits forever when stdin is left open. Pass -m and close stdin in scripts.

tools.name: Pi
tools.pricing: Free, open source (MIT); you pay for your own model API usage
tools.description: Minimal, extensible open-source terminal coding agent (read, bash, edit and write tools, plus extensions, skills and print/JSON/RPC modes); works with many model providers.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 50 s with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote all four files in 6 model requests, then a 7th request (a quick self-check) hit the free tier's per-minute request limit and Pi stopped without retrying, so there was no final summary. Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, labelled input, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state, correct README. -1 DX: needs Node 22.19+ (one extra step on our Node 20 machine). -1 DX: no final summary and no retry after the rate-limit error.

tools.name: Crush
tools.pricing: Free, source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT); you pay for your own model API usage (Charm's own Hyper provider has a free tier but needs sign-in)
tools.description: Charm's open terminal coding agent (Crush CLI) that works with many model providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter and more).

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 646 s (17 model requests, no interventions) on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote its own Node test, caught and fixed a counter bug before finishing. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label is always 'Mark task complete'. -1 speed: took about 11 minutes (slow model responses). -1 DX: short final summary and a .crush/ data folder left in the project. Checker note: the original checker missed the counter because the number and label are separate flex items; checker v1.1 fixes this for every tool (all earlier scores unchanged).

tools.name: Cursor
tools.description: AI-first code editor with an agent that can plan, edit and run code across your project.

test.evidence: Retest on the latest CLI (first test Oct 15 on 2026.10.14-941492e also scored 97). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 44 s with 1 prompt and no interventions on a free Cursor account, same default model. It now validates saved data field by field, so a corrupted localStorage value no longer breaks the app (we checked). -1 quality: task IDs still use crypto.randomUUID(), which fails outside secure contexts (we checked: served over plain http on a LAN address, adding a task throws and nothing is added). -1: the checkbox and delete-button accessibility labels are generic ('Mark task complete', 'Delete task') and don't name the task. -1 DX: separate browser login step.

tools.name: Cline
tools.pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage)
tools.description: Open-source autonomous coding agent that runs inside VS Code.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks. First attempt hit Gemini high demand (no files); re-run completed the app in 312 s (then hit the free-tier 20-request/day quota after Cline's own self-test passed, before a final summary). Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent escaping, dynamic aria-labels. Speed −3 for the high-demand re-run. DX −2: no final summary because of quota.

tools.name: Aider
tools.pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage)
tools.description: Open-source AI pair programmer that edits code in your local git repo from the terminal.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks in 26 s (1 model request, no interventions). -3 quality: README cut off and 2 stray files created from README code snippets. -3 DX: pip install failed on Python 3.13 (worked with Python 3.12) and the stray files.

tools.name: Bolt.new
tools.referral_note: Referral link: we may earn a commission and you get 20% off; it never affects scores or rankings.
tools.description: Browser-based AI app builder that generates, runs and deploys full-stack web apps from prompts.

test.tool_version: Bolt.new web app (Free plan, Standard mode)
test.model: Bolt.new default model (Free plan; model name not shown)
test.evidence: Passed 10/10 checks in about 2 minutes with 1 prompt and no interventions on the Free plan. 9 checks verified in Bolt's live preview; the reload/persistence check (C8) was verified on the exported project because the preview did not come back after a page reload. -2 quality: left Vite starter files (package.json, package-lock.json, .bolt) and an unused escapeHtml function. -2: no accessibility labels on the input, checkbox or icon-only delete button. -2 DX: the preview showed a stale starter page until refreshed and broke on reload.

tools.name: Goose
tools.pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage
tools.description: Open-source, extensible AI agent (desktop app, CLI and API) from the Agentic AI Foundation, originally built by Block; works with many model providers.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. All four files were written within 18.5 minutes (6 model requests), but Gemini 'high demand' errors and slow responses meant Goose had not posted its final reply when our 20-minute timebox ended, so we scored the files present at the cutoff and counted the full 20 minutes. Quality 25: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state. -5 speed: 20 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: no final summary before the cutoff.

tools.name: Kilo Code
tools.pricing: Free, open source (MIT) for individuals; free models via Auto Free with no account, or pay as you go, bring your own key, or Kilo Pass; Teams $15/user/month
tools.description: Open-source agentic coding assistant for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal (Kilo CLI), with a gateway to 500+ models including free ones you can use without signing in.

test.model: Kilo Auto Free (routed to reflection/beam-free; no account, no API key)
test.evidence: Retest on the same CLI version and the same Auto Free setting (first test Oct 26 scored 96). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 13 s with no interventions, no sign-in, no API key and no card; Auto Free picked reflection/beam-free this time. The app it wrote was weaker than on Oct 26: -1 quality: an unused escapeHtml helper again. -1: saved data is read with no error handling, so a corrupted localStorage value stops the whole app (we checked: nothing can be added). -1: no checkbox; you toggle a task by clicking its text, which can't be reached with the keyboard. -1: the text input has no label (placeholder only). -1: the delete button just says 'Delete'. -1 DX: the final summary was again just 'Done.'. Note: Auto Free chooses the model for you and can change over time, so results can vary between runs; Kilo says it may route to providers that log prompts, so don't use it for private code.

tools.name: Qwen Code
tools.pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage (the free Qwen OAuth tier ended 2026-04-15)
tools.description: Open-source terminal coding agent from Alibaba's Qwen team (originally forked from Gemini CLI); works with OpenAI-, Anthropic- and Gemini-compatible providers and has a headless mode for scripts and CI.

test.evidence: Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier and ended with a clear summary, but took 18 minutes: Gemini was slow and returned 6 'high demand' errors (Qwen Code retried them itself), and the agent spent 4 extra requests reading files that did not exist yet. Quality 23: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, correct README. -1 the text input has no label (placeholder only); -1 checkbox and delete labels don't name the task. -4 speed: 18 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: needs Node 22+ and a hand-written settings file to use a Gemini key headlessly.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.pricing: Paid Claude plan or Anthropic API usage
tools.description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool that works in your terminal, IDE and codebase.

tools.description: OpenAI's coding agent across ChatGPT, the cloud, the IDE extension and the terminal.

tools.description: Cloud development platform whose Replit Agent builds and deploys apps from a prompt.
tools.status: Untested: login blocked from our test machine

tools.description: AI code editor with an agentic assistant (Cascade) for multi-file changes.
tools.test_note: Windsurf sign-up now goes through Devin (Cognition), and the free Devin account reported its free credits as already used up, so no task could run at $0. No score.

tools.description: Fast open-source code editor with built-in AI agent editing.
tools.status: Untested: agent runs only in the desktop app

new_this_week.name: agent-manager
new_this_week.description: Local terminal app (tmux TUI) that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Pi, Cursor CLI and other coding-agent CLIs side by side with live status, project groups, diff review and fork sessions. Uses your existing installs and subscriptions. Apache-2.0; brew install agent-manager (macOS/Linux); Scoop on Windows. About 650 stars / 70 forks as of Nov 7. Disclosed: not a sandbox; each session is your own CLI as-is.

new_this_week.name: Stroq
new_this_week.description: Local audit and guard for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions: finds known secrets that left your machine, then installs local hooks that trace risky commands back to the text that dictated them. Apache-2.0; npx @stroq/cli; no account, no telemetry (writes a small cache under ~/.stroq). Show HN Nov 5 (~90 pts). About 200 stars. Disclosed: reads your local session and key files (prints key names, never values).

new_this_week.name: sand3d
new_this_week.description: Python library for writing 3D objects as short programs over Blender's bpy, built so an LLM can author parts, joints and assemblies in a few hundred tokens (the whole API fits in about 3,600 tokens). Exports GLB, URDF, USDA, OBJ and STL; deterministic bit-for-bit meshes. Apache-2.0, free; created Nov 3, about 500 stars. Docs and gallery at sand3d.sandflow.ai; Hugging Face explorer. Needs Python 3.11/3.13 (bpy comes with it). Disclosed: you bring the model that writes the sand3d programs.

new_this_week.name: LivLiv Player
new_this_week.description: Lightweight 2.5D character player for the web (~30 KB gzipped core, WebGL2, no dependencies): lip sync from mic/audio/video and optional webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), one API for LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters, plus 21 featured characters ready to drop in. Apache-2.0, free npm package @livliv-dev/player; created Nov 4, about 700 stars. Live demo at livliv-dev.github.io/player. Disclosed: face tracking pulls in @mediapipe/tasks-vision only when you import it.

new_this_week.name: pixel-gif-sticker-pack
new_this_week.description: Codex / Claude Code skill that turns a character reference into a chat GIF sticker pack (or a short mascot brand film): pixel, illustration or photographic looks, light-motion or articulated actions, with local Python/Pillow exporters and a visual review gate. MIT, free; created Nov 5, about 510 stars, 242 example stickers in-repo. Disclosed: new pose art uses whatever image model your agent already has; the exporters themselves need no API key.

new_this_week.name: Zerg Client
new_this_week.description: Coding-agent harness (ztc) that owns its own terminal multiplexer: ask for Vim or htop and panes open beside the agent; panes can hold more agents on different models. Evaluation beta on Product Hunt Nov 5; desktop/interactive client for Mac Apple silicon (v0.11.0-beta.1), headless on macOS/Linux/Windows. Free to evaluate under the Zerg Source Available License; sign in with ZergAI or bring your own OpenAI/DeepSeek key. Disclosed: not open source; ongoing commercial use needs a separate license; model usage billed separately; Windows/Linux desktop apps still "coming soon".

new_this_week.name: Rerun
new_this_week.description: Self-hostable open-source AI coworkers (AGPL-3.0): a Foreman plans a team, each coworker gets its own memory, skills and computer, and they ask before sending, paying or deleting. Works with Gmail, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear and 200+ other tools (plus any MCP server), on an API key or the Claude/ChatGPT subscription you already pay for. Docker Compose self-host (docs.rerun.build/self-host) or Rerun Cloud. Product Hunt Nov 5; GitHub repo from Oct 29, about 694 stars and v0.7.0 on Nov 4. Disclosed: needs your own model access; first self-host build wants ~6 GB RAM / 40 GB disk and a free Supabase project.

new_this_week.name: Cinecode
new_this_week.description: Claude Code / Cursor skill that makes short films, long YouTube videos, ads, explainers and music videos as code: the agent writes the script, builds every frame in three.js (or 2D/paint/ink looks), designs the sound and hands you a finished MP4 rendered in headless Chrome. MIT, free; created Nov 3, about 330 GitHub stars. Needs Node 22+, Python 3, ffmpeg and Chrome on your machine; optional narrator uses your own Gemini free-tier key, ElevenLabs or a free Turkish voice. Install is a git clone into ~/.claude/skills (or Cursor skills), not a curl | sh.

new_this_week.name: Sketchy
new_this_week.description: Layout engine for AI diagrams: the model says what to draw and label; Sketchy places parts, routes wires and walks you through steps. Hand-drawn interactive drawings in Claude chat (skill zip) or as an MCP server in Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code — systems, CS/ML concepts, your own repo (click a box to open the file), Arduino/ESP32 circuits and labeled photos. MIT, free; Product Hunt Nov 4, v0.1.8 Nov 3, about 196 GitHub stars. Local photo labeling uses Florence-2 on your computer.

new_this_week.name: OpenMail
new_this_week.description: Email API and inboxes built for AI agents: each agent gets its own address on your domain (or openmail.sh), replies arrive over webhook or WebSocket, attachments land as plain text, and there is a hosted MCP server plus Hermes / Claude Code / CLI plugins. Product Hunt Nov 4. Free plan with no card: 3 inboxes, 3,000 emails/month, 3 GB (OpenMail footer on Free). Pro from €9/mo. Built and hosted in the EU. Disclosed: SaaS, not open source; Free has a daily send cap.

new_this_week.name: Agent Autoloop
new_this_week.description: Runs Claude Code, Codex or any command-line agent that takes a prompt and prints a reply in the background on your Mac or Linux machine: cron jobs, new GitHub issues and error reports become tasks. When the agent needs your call (deleting data, spending money, messaging someone) it sends a card to Slack, Discord, Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom or a desktop notification and exits, so no tokens burn while it waits; your answer resumes the same session. Small zero-dependency TypeScript kernel, everything else is a plugin. MIT, free; v1.0.0 released Nov 3 and about 1,650 GitHub stars in its first day. Needs Node 24 and an agent you're already signed in to. README is Chinese-first with an English version, and the one-line installer is a curl | sh script, so read it before you run it.

new_this_week.name: Three-Live (Google)
new_this_week.description: Open-source runtime from Google that takes AI-generated Three.js code, runs it in a sandbox with time and memory limits, and renders it natively: WebGL2 and WebXR on the web, Filament and Scene Viewer on Android, RealityKit and Quick Look on iOS and visionOS. Its browser playgrounds edit scenes and export GLB, USDZ and AR in one tap with no build. Apache-2.0, free; introduced on the Google Open Source Blog Nov 3 (v1.2.0). Developer preview (alpha) and "not an officially supported Google product"; you bring the model that writes the Three.js.

new_this_week.name: Recto
new_this_week.description: Free desktop design canvas for coding agents (Mac, Windows, Linux): it detects Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode on your machine and runs them inside the app, so you can prompt a UI, motion, SVG or 3D design, then drag, resize and restyle it with the mouse, pin comments for the agent and reprompt. Designs are real HTML and CSS you can export; no MCP or API setup, everything runs locally. Shown on Show HN Nov 3 (v0.1.6, released Oct 29). Early: the app is not open source, its terms page is still "coming soon", and you need your own coding agent.

new_this_week.name: Claude Animated Shorts
new_this_week.description: Claude Code skill that makes 55-70 second vertical cartoon story shorts (2D characters in a painted 3D world, gliding cameras, synthesized music and sound effects) by writing a three.js scene and rendering it with Remotion on your own PC, with no AI video generator. Ships the full source of its example short. MIT, free; created Nov 1 and past 850 GitHub stars in two days. You need Node, Python, ffmpeg and Remotion (Remotion has its own license: free for individuals and small teams, larger companies need a paid license), and you bring your own voice-over.

new_this_week.name: UNCUT
new_this_week.description: A 7 MB headless coding-agent harness for scripts, CI and experiments: one static Go binary, four tools (read, write, replace, run a command), plain stdin/stdout or NDJSON events. It never summarizes or trims context, and stops with an error instead of passing off a cut-off answer as success. Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or a local model, no telemetry. MIT, free; v0.1 released Nov 2, about 580 GitHub stars. Not a sandbox: shell commands run as your user, so use a container for untrusted tasks.

new_this_week.name: Flockbay
new_this_week.description: Desktop AI game maker built on the official Godot engine (Windows, macOS, Linux): its AI writes GDScript and scenes into a normal Godot 4 project on your disk, runs and playtests the game and fixes what breaks, and Claude Code, Codex or Cursor can drive it over MCP. Launched on Product Hunt Nov 2. Free download with no card; free hosted AI to start (needs an account) or free on your own Claude/ChatGPT plan or API key; paid plans from $20/month add hosted usage. The app itself is not open source.

new_this_week.name: pixelfx (patch.gg)
new_this_week.description: 244 pixel-art effects and animations for games (fire, explosions, magic, weather, UI, pickups, critters), each a small piece of code: play them in the browser gallery, recolor and mirror them, drop them into a browser game or export sprite sheets for Godot, Unity or any engine. Ships a Claude Code skill that drafts, renders, looks at and refines new effects. MIT, free; open-sourced Oct 30 and past 3,000 GitHub stars in two days. Live gallery at patch-gg.github.io/pixelfx.

new_this_week.name: stack-diagram
new_this_week.description: Agent skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other skills-compatible agents: describe your stack in one sentence and get an architecture diagram with the official vendor logos, as a single HTML file, PNG or React component. MIT, free, no account; it fetches logos from public icon libraries. It offers to post your diagram to a public gallery, but only if you say yes. Released Nov 1, 760+ stars in its first day.

new_this_week.name: teardown
new_this_week.description: Claude Code skill that turns any machine into an interactive 3D simulator you can take apart: ask how an engine, watch or excavator arm works and it builds one offline three.js page with live readouts and a guided tour, plus optional 60 fps video export. MIT, free skill (needs Node 20+; ffmpeg for video). Three example machines included. Created Oct 30, 1,000+ stars.

new_this_week.name: Video to Game (fal)
new_this_week.description: Agent skill (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini) that turns a short AI-generated gameplay video into a playable single-file Three.js browser game: it studies the frames, generates matching images, 3D models and sounds, then plays its own game to check it. MIT; 31 example games you can play. The skill is free, but asset generation runs on fal's paid API (the author reports about $6 per game).

new_this_week.name: Grim Prompter (Jim Manico)
new_this_week.description: Threat modeling for AI coding agents from a well-known app-security trainer: run /threat-model in Claude Code or $threat-model in Codex for a read-only review with findings cited to file and line, plus a mode for reviewing a branch. 36 architecture workflows and 29 method prompts. MIT, free.

new_this_week.name: Overtone captions
new_this_week.description: Caption files that re-cut themselves for 16:9 and 9:16 video, with a CLI and a video.js plugin. Re-cutting existing subtitles works offline with no key; transcription uses OpenAI/Azure keys or runs locally with whisper.cpp and Ollama. Handy for devlogs and trailers. MIT.

new_this_week.name: Floorplan
new_this_week.description: Claude Code / Codex plugin that reads your codebase and draws an interactive, plain-English map of every part, file and web request, then shows which parts the agent touched after each change. MIT, zero dependencies, runs locally with no telemetry; questions go through your own Claude or Codex account. Live demo at haydenschmitty.github.io/floorplan-demo. Created Oct 27, 2026 (v0.2.2 Oct 29).

new_this_week.name: MCode Stack (MiniMax)
new_this_week.description: The MiniMax Code team's own open-sourced workflows: 17 SKILL.md skills and checklists (independent review, subagent-split check, long-session check, small PRs, tool-budget audit and more). MIT; installs as a plugin marketplace in Claude Code or Codex, or copies into ~/.agents/skills. Released Oct 28, 2026.

new_this_week.name: DevBox (RudderStack)
new_this_week.description: Self-hosted autonomous engineering harness: hand it a ticket (CLI or Linear) and it plans, codes, runs tests, reviews its own diff and opens a draft PR, one sandbox per task with placeholder tokens swapped in by an egress proxy. MIT; runs on Docker Compose or Kubernetes with your own OpenAI or Anthropic key (model usage is billed by your provider). Open-sourced Oct 27, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Our Silly Games
new_this_week.description: Make a browser game by chatting with Claude Code or Codex, then publish it with free hosting, realtime multiplayer and leaderboards. MIT plugin (kirkness/osg-plugin) with 11 game-making skills; publishing needs a free Our Silly Games sign-in. Product Hunt Oct 27, 2026.

new_this_week.name: trompe + anymove (patch.gg)
new_this_week.description: Two Apache-2.0 game-art pipelines from patch.gg: trompe textures a whole gray-box game level with image models (glTF out), and anymove (github.com/patch-gg/anymove) turns one AI video into a GLB animation for any rigged creature. Code is free; the image/video models run on paid APIs (their demo level cost about $4.44 on fal). Released Oct 25 and 27, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Nyxis
new_this_week.description: Lean backend framework for apps written by AI agents: you write and approve Cedar authorization policies, the agent writes handlers, and every build checks a formal proof that no request sequence can leak or modify data beyond permissions. MIT, v0.1, under active development. Created Oct 26, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Hob
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) desktop app that runs open-weight models like Gemma and gpt-oss on your own computer, as an offline, private alternative to Claude and ChatGPT; no account or subscription. FrigadeHQ/hob; Show HN Oct 26 (144 pts), v0.2 released Oct 26. Mac, Windows, Linux.

new_this_week.name: desigma
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT/Apache-2.0), offline Figma alternative written in Rust, with a local MCP server so coding agents can inspect designs, edit them and generate code; imports Figma files. Early alpha (first release Oct 11); Product Hunt #9 on Oct 26.

new_this_week.name: GEOInflow
new_this_week.description: Self-hosted analytics (MIT) that shows which AI crawlers and AI search engines visit your site, which pages they request or miss, and what traffic AI search sends you. Open-sourced Oct 26, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Corgi
new_this_week.description: Terminal multiplexer for humans and coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenCode): shows which agent is working or needs you, keeps sessions running like tmux, tracks tokens and file changes. MIT (tals/corgi); Show HN Oct 23 (138 pts). macOS, Linux, WSL.

new_this_week.name: Farol
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source CLI and GitHub Action that maps the risk of a pull request after AI review: riskiest files, what they reach, diff coverage and contract breaks (TS/React, Go, Python). MIT (winnin/farol); Show HN Oct 25.

new_this_week.name: AgentValley
new_this_week.description: Free macOS notch app that shows every Claude Code session and sub-agent at a glance (model, working or waiting on you), each with a pixel programmer. MIT (morsechimwai/agent-valley); Product Hunt #4 on Oct 24.

new_this_week.name: tstack (Theo / t3dotgg)
new_this_week.description: Theo's everyday agent skills for Claude Code and Codex: full-send PR flow, multi-model 'council' review, babysit-PR through CI, take over someone else's PR. MIT; published Oct 24. Needs an authenticated gh CLI.

new_this_week.name: BeautifulRust
new_this_week.description: Claude Code plugin that teaches Claude to write idiomatic, robust Rust. MIT; created Oct 23, 900+ stars in its first days.

new_this_week.name: xss-audit skill
new_this_week.description: Agent skill that runs a 14-layer static XSS audit on React, TypeScript and JavaScript projects. MIT; created Oct 24. A useful second check on AI-written front-end code.

new_this_week.name: Halv
new_this_week.description: Desktop workspace that runs Claude Code, Codex, Kimi and GLM side by side on the plans you already pay for, with a local proxy that trims context tokens and a live savings meter. The app and its local engine went open source (Apache-2.0) on Oct 22; only the optional Halv Cloud router is paid. macOS first; Show HN Oct 22.

new_this_week.name: Recursive Flint + rec
new_this_week.description: Flint is a local coding model from Recursive with open weights on Hugging Face (Apache-2.0); rec is its Apache-2.0 inference engine with ready-made launchers for Pi and OpenCode. Needs an Apple Silicon M4 Pro/M5 Pro/M5 Max with 48 GB+ memory. Released Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Rossark Motion skill
new_this_week.description: Claude Code skill that turns any SVG drawing into a smooth 60 fps animation (breathing, blinking, full-body acting, whole scenes) in React Native and SwiftUI. Handy for app and game illustrations. MIT; created Oct 22, trending on GitHub.

new_this_week.name: 3D Model Anything (Wes Bos)
new_this_week.description: iPhone LiDAR + photo capture app, a Three.js viewer and a scan-to-threejs agent skill that guides a coding agent through rebuilding a real room as an editable 3D scene. Good fit for game devs and Three.js tinkerers. Code MIT (demo assets under a separate license); created Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Omnara
new_this_week.description: Open-source, self-hostable server for durable agents: create an agent with an API call and Omnara runs the loop, sandboxes, secrets and permissions, with state in Postgres so agents survive restarts. Your laptop or a cloud sandbox can join as a machine. Apache-2.0; hosted version at omnara.com. Show HN Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Harp
new_this_week.description: Unofficial fork of the Warp terminal with a sidebar for running many Claude Code and Codex sessions side by side: shows which agent is working, waiting for you or done, plus usage-limit rings. macOS, free, AGPL-3.0. Created Oct 20, trending on GitHub.

new_this_week.name: durable-harness (Vercel)
new_this_week.description: Runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi or your own coding agent as a durable session that logs every model and tool call and resumes after crashes or timeouts. Open source (Apache-2.0) from Vercel Labs; announced Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: BAND for Developers
new_this_week.description: Shared chat rooms where coding agents and people collaborate, with governance over how agents talk to each other. Free plan for personal, non-commercial use (up to 20 remote agents); Pro $17.99/mo. Product Hunt #2 on Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: SuperCMO AI
new_this_week.description: Open-source agent skills that turn Claude Code, Cursor or Codex into a marketing team for your product: learns your brand, studies competitor ads, writes copy and makes UGC, product and image ads, asking before anything expensive renders. Apache-2.0; bring your own model keys or pay per use. Product Hunt Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Opposable
new_this_week.description: Free Android app that lets Claude, ChatGPT or Codex operate your phone's apps, with an on-device 2B screen model (GUI-Owl 1.5, 1.5 GB download) as an offline fallback. Show HN Oct 21.

new_this_week.name: Reticle
new_this_week.description: Makes your coding agent verify its own work: drives the running app, reads network calls, state and console, and returns pass/fail/cannot tell with the file:line to fix. SDK Apache-2.0, server source-available (FSL); free to start, no card. Show HN Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: fx0 (Vercel)
new_this_week.description: Vercel's open-source design agent: describe a page and it writes one HTML file, built on the durable libfx agent loop. Apache-2.0 (vercel-labs/fx0); hosted demo has a few free prompts, or self-host with your own AI Gateway.

new_this_week.name: Nimbalyst Wiki
new_this_week.description: A local markdown wiki your coding agents write and keep updated (decisions, open questions, the big picture). Free MIT plugin + MCP server for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and other MCP agents; no account. Product Hunt Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: MCP Census
new_this_week.description: Checks public evidence for an MCP server before you install it and returns PASS / REVIEW / BLOCK / UNKNOWN (a first gate, not a malware scan). 10 free lookups/day with no signup; free account 1,000 credits/month. Show HN Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: Pando
new_this_week.description: Self-hosted platform to deploy and share apps your team builds with AI, each behind access control from the start. Open source (AGPL-3.0); paid commercial license/hosting optional. Show HN Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: Triage by Chodeberg
new_this_week.description: Users file bug reports from their AI assistant into a live copy of your CLI/TUI/Linux app; Triage replays each on a clean machine and only forwards the ones that reproduce. Free 100 credits/month, then pay per minute. Product Hunt Oct 20.

new_this_week.name: Hermes GameForge
new_this_week.description: Game-dev plugin for the Hermes agent: generates SFX, music, NPC voices, sprites, tilesets and low-poly 3D models offline, scaffolds web/Godot/Unity builds and runs a playtester bot. MIT; brand-new (Oct 21) and not reviewed by us yet.

new_this_week.name: buddylist
new_this_week.description: Free desktop app (Mac, Windows, Linux) that puts Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and OpenCode in an MSN-style buddy list: group chats, separate Git worktrees, diffs and PR checks. Bring your own agent accounts. Product Hunt #8 and Show HN, Oct 19, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Craig
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) terminal UI that runs Claude Code, Codex and Cursor agents in parallel, each task in its own Git worktree, from task to PR. npm install, no account. Show HN, Oct 19, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Quorus
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) local relay where Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode agents join one room over MCP, fix in their own worktrees and review each other's work. Demo runs on free OpenCode models. Show HN, Oct 19, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Spotnote
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) Vite plugin: click any element in your running app, write what should change, and hand your coding agent the exact file, line and column. Local only, no account. Show HN, Oct 19, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Lights-on software factory
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) boilerplate for running Claude Code as a 'software factory': sandbox container, deterministic command regulator, linter hooks and a workflow generator that the author says cut token spend about 80%. Show HN, Oct 20, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Sphinx
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source (MIT) git hook for agent-assisted coding: before you push, it quizzes you on what your AI agent's changes actually do. Show HN, Oct 18, 2026.

new_this_week.name: WhatsApp MCP (Cloudflare)
new_this_week.description: Open-source (MIT), read-only MCP server that lets your AI agent search and read your own WhatsApp messages; runs on Cloudflare Workers' free tier. Show HN, Oct 18, 2026.

new_this_week.name: llmspeed
new_this_week.description: Free, open-source web tool that simulates how fast a local LLM would run (tokens/sec, time to first token) on a given GPU or Mac before you buy hardware. Show HN, Oct 17, 2026.

new_this_week.name: withHuman
new_this_week.description: Open-source human approval layer for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, LangGraph and more). Intercepts tool calls; self-host or hosted. Product Hunt launch Oct 15, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Navige
new_this_week.description: Sits between agents and paid models/tools to cut runaway spend (routing, cache, loop guards). Free start. Product Hunt #2 on Oct 15, 2026.

new_this_week.name: Tiden
new_this_week.description: Intent verification for coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Copilot). Specs versioned like code; 14-day free trial. Live with install script.

new_this_week.name: Graphicle
new_this_week.description: Local Rust code-graph + memory for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, MCP). No account. Apache-2.0. Show HN Oct 14, 2026.

new_this_week.name: OpenUI 1.0
new_this_week.description: Open standard for generative UI (React/Vue/Svelte/Angular runtimes). MIT on GitHub (thesysdev/openui). Useful for agent-built interfaces.
